note: Both sets cover the same core facts (dishwasher capacity, 120°F/115°F thresholds, two sensors, heated-drying disablement, clothes-drying eligibility and the Figure 8 scoring bands) and both are heavily padded with duplicate restatements of the same facts under different entity/attribute names. Set A additionally garbles one quote ('at least one wash and rinse and cycle' instead of 'wash and rinse cycle'), while Set B's quotes are all faithful. Set B also has slightly fewer duplicate pairs (7 vs 8), making it marginally cleaner and more accurate overall.
remarks: Both sets miss several substantive facts on the page: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of the two sensor readings, or the lower if the higher sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption' (8-5e), cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal (8-5f), the allowed load states (empty/partial/full, soiled or clean, 8-5h), the two-loads-per-day requirement and separate scoring of each load (item d), and the requirement that towel-visible drying methods be demonstrated to the architecture and market appeal juries (item c). Both sets also duplicate the same facts under two entity names (e.g., 'Clothes Dryer Subcontest' vs 'clothes-drying task'; 'dishwasher' vs 'Dishwasher'), inflating claim counts without adding information.
